Thermostat Set the system to Off at the thermostat and wait until the blower stops before you open a filter slot. This does not disconnect electricity. Don’t take the thermostat off the wall. Air filter Use only a tool-free filter slot or return grille your owner’s manual names, reachable from the floor. Keep furnace and air-handler doors closed. Read it without opening the furnace Most furnaces have a small window in the lower door, or a display, or a code on the thermostat. Look only. Don’t remove the door. On some brands, cutting power or taking the door off erases the stored code. Watch for one full minute. Codes repeat, with a pause between them. Count short flashes and long flashes separately. chunks.title: Furnace Running but Blowing Cold Air
chunks.text: Furnace Running but Blowing Cold Air. What to check when the blower runs and the air isn’t warm, or when no air comes out of the vents. The blower can be running while the air stays cool, or the vents can be quiet because the blower isn’t running. The checks overlap, and the ending doesn’t. Air is moving, and it isn’t warm Look at the thermostat you already use. Don’t take it off the wall. Set mode to Heat, fan to Auto, and the setpoint a few degrees above the room temperature. Fan On blows room-temperature air between heating cycles, which can feel cold. Some thermostats wait a few minutes before they start. Wait one full heating cycle before you decide the air is cold. The blower often starts before the burner, and the first minute can feel cool.

chunks.title: What Size Furnace Filter Do I Need?
chunks.text: What Size Furnace Filter Do I Need?. Where furnace filters sit, how to read the size on the frame, and how often to check it. Home › Answers › Furnace filter size What Size Furnace Filter Do I Need? Last updated October 29, 2026. The size is printed on the filter’s frame, not guessed from the furnace brand. It is three numbers: length, width, and thickness. Buy that size. A thicker filter than the slot can crush the media or keep the door from closing, and the furnace may not run. Where to look A slot on the furnace or air handler. A cover on the side, bottom, or top slides or lifts by hand. The filter is in that slot, not in the burner compartment. A return grille. In a hallway, wall, or ceiling, the filter sits behind a grille that opens by hand. That’s the filter for some systems.

Put the thermostat back to Heat or Cool and the fan to Auto. How often ENERGY STAR says to check the filter every month in heavy-use seasons. If it looks dirty after a month, change it. At a minimum, change it every 3 months. Pets, smoke, and a renovation clog a filter sooner. Your owner’s manual wins if it gives a different interval.

Checks you can do Look at the thermostat you already use. Don’t take it off the wall. Set mode to Heat, fan to Auto, and the setpoint a few degrees above the room temperature. Fan On blows room-temperature air between heating cycles, which can feel cold. Some thermostats wait a few minutes before they start. Then wait one full cycle. Don’t change installer settings such as cycles per hour to force it to stay on. Turn the system Off at the thermostat and wait until the blower stops. That does not cut power. A smell only when hot water runs is a water problem. Safety first: If you smell gas, leave now and call the gas utility or 911 from outside. If a CO alarm sounds, get everyone outside and call 911. If hot water or steam is spraying from the heater or its relief pipe, stay back. For a serious burn, call 911.

chunks.text: Hot Water Smells Like Rotten Eggs? Here’s Why. The usual cause of a sulfur smell in hot water only, and when to call a pro. If you smell gas, leave first. If the house was empty two weeks or more, run a hot tap at a sink first for several minutes before the dishwasher or washer, with no flame or spark nearby: makers warn hydrogen gas can build up (Rheem gas Use & Care p. 18). Don’t remove the anode or add bleach or chemicals to the tank. Makers say the tank needs an anode; Rheem says running without one greatly shortens tank life and voids warranty (p. 21). chunks.text: Water Heater Maintenance Checklist. Manual-based water heater checks you can do yourself, and what a pro service should include. Following a checklist here does not keep, protect, or extend a warranty. Most water heater care is set by your owner’s manual. Here is what it asks for, what you can do yourself, and exactly why the rest is a plumber’s job. Pick a time you’ll remember. Your manual sets how often. Water hardness Your water’s hardness changes how often some heaters need care, but the schedule comes from your owner’s manual, not from a hardness label alone. On city water, look up your utility’s yearly water quality report (often called a Consumer Confidence Report) and find “hardness.” It may be in grains per gallon (gpg) or in ppm or mg/L.

chunks.text: Water Heater Maintenance Checklist. Manual-based water heater checks you can do yourself, and what a pro service should include. On a well, or if the report doesn’t list it, use a hardness test strip from a hardware store, following the package directions. Soft, moderately hard, hard, and very hard are plain-language categories from the U.S. Geological Survey for describing water (TRADE). They are not a service schedule. If you have a water softener, some manuals ask for more frequent anode checks — follow your owner’s manual. For flush, descale, and anode timing, follow your owner’s manual. Look around Once in a while, look without touching: water on the floor or in the pan, drips from the relief pipe’s end, rust at the fittings or top of the tank, or new popping sounds. Outside, check that vents aren’t blo…

chunks.title: Water Heater Maintenance Checklist
chunks.text: Water Heater Maintenance Checklist. Manual-based water heater checks you can do yourself, and what a pro service should include. If you smell gas, leave the house now and call the gas utility or 911 from outside. If you see any of the other signs, start a guided check. Relief valve If your manual tells you to test the relief valve, we’ll walk you through it. If it doesn’t, leave the valve alone. Start the guided check and choose Water heater. Heat pump water heater filter Heat pump water heaters have an air filter on top. Clean it when the filter light comes on, as your manual shows. Tank flush Sediment settles at the bottom of a tank, more so with hard water. Your manual asks for a yearly flush. We don’t guide this one: it means draining very hot water through a valve that can clog open, and on gas or elect…

Plug electric space heaters into a wall, clear of anything that burns. Don't turn it back on until you know why it's off.

chunks.title: Main shutoff closed
chunks.text: Main shutoff closed. You’ve limited the water. Leave the valve closed and call a licensed plumber or water heater professional. Leave the valve closed and call a licensed plumber or water heater professional. Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

chunks.title: Minimum flow
chunks.text: Minimum flow. Tankless heaters start heating only above a minimum flow. Makers’ minimum flows: Navien at least 0.5 gal/min (NPE-2 manual, p. 15); Noritz NCC199CDV starts at 0.5 GPM and can keep running down to 0.29 GPM (Owner’s Guide, pp. 39, 46). If every faucet is weak, the problem is upstream: a clogged inlet filter, scale in the heater or a supply valve. Those need the water shut off and parts opened. Open the hot tap more. Use the hot side only — a mixing valve set towa…

chunks.title: Report the affected fixture
chunks.text: Report the affected fixture. A problem at one fixture can involve its mixing control or plumbing. This does not confirm the water heater works. Tell a plumber which fixtures are affected and whether the issue is recent. Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

chunks.title: Have the pilot problem checked
chunks.text: Have the pilot problem checked. An extinguished pilot needs an equipment-specific inspection. Gas parts need a gas-qualified pro and leak testing. Call the gas utility or a licensed water heater professional. If a smell appears, leave the house now and call the gas utility or 911 from outside. Do not relight it. Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

chunks.title: Book an anode check
chunks.text: Book an anode check. The anode rod is a metal rod that slowly wears away so the tank metal doesn’t. Your manual says how often to have it checked (for some models, every year). Checking it means taking it out of the tank, so we leave it to a plumber. Ask them how much core wire is showing. Your manual lists when it should be replaced. If a heat pump water heater shows an anode alarm, call a licensed plumber or water heater professional. Clearing that alarm is only for after…

chunks.title: Book a descale
chunks.text: Book a descale. Hard water leaves scale inside a tankless heater. When your heater shows a service code for this, or your manual says it’s time, book a descale. The heater needs service valves on its water lines for this. If yours has none, a plumber can add them. Descaling means closing and opening four valves in the right order and pumping a cleaning solution through the heater. A wrong valve sends the solution into your pipes or hot water at the heater. The maker calls it…

chunks.title: Book a tank flush
chunks.text: Book a tank flush. Sediment settles at the bottom of a tank, more so with hard water. Your manual asks for a yearly flush. We don’t guide this one: it means draining very hot water through a valve that can clog open, and on gas or electric tanks it means shutting off and restoring the heat source. Book a plumber to flush the tank. Draining means hot water through a valve that sediment can jam open, and refilling before power or gas comes back. An electric element powered in…

chunks.title: Find your water hardness
chunks.text: Find your water hardness. Your water’s hardness changes how often some heaters need care, but the schedule comes from your owner’s manual, not from a hardness label alone. On city water, look up your utility’s yearly water quality report (often called a Consumer Confidence Report) and find “hardness.” It may be in grains per gallon (gpg) or in ppm or mg/L. On a well, or if the report doesn’t list it, use a hardness test strip from a hardware store, following the package dire…

chunks.title: Book the inlet screen with the descale
chunks.text: Book the inlet screen with the descale. Your tankless heater has a small screen where cold water comes in. If it clogs, you may get less hot water or an error code. Cleaning it means draining the heater, so book it with your descale. The filter sits in the water line under pressure. Reaching it means shutting the water off and draining the heater. A pinched or missing seal leaks when the water comes back on. Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves,…

chunks.title: What a pro service visit should include
chunks.text: What a pro service visit should include. A water heater service visit should list what was done. For a tank: flush, anode checked against your manual’s replacement rule, relief valve checked, and for gas, the burner, venting and gas connections. For tankless: descale, inlet filter, venting, and the error history read (not cleared). For a heat pump model: filter, condensate drain and the system checked for alerts. Ask for the results in writing. Ask for the results in writing…

chunks.title: Leave power controls as they are
chunks.text: Leave power controls as they are. A dark display or possible trip needs professional investigation. Call a licensed water heater professional or electrician. Report whether a breaker or GFCI appeared tripped. Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

chunks.title: Record the delay and recirculation settings
chunks.text: Record the delay and recirculation settings. Pipe distance, demand, and recirculation setup can affect the wait. The cause has not been confirmed. Photograph the normal user display and record when the delay happens. Use the exact manual or installer for recirculation and mode changes; do not enter installer menus. Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

chunks.title: Record demand and recovery
chunks.text: Record demand and recovery. A tank reheats from cold after heavy use. Check again after the recovery time your manual lists, or later the same day. Use the recovery information in your exact owner’s manual. If the problem occurs under ordinary demand, contact a professional. Do not raise temperature as a workaround. Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

chunks.title: Keep clear of the relief discharge
chunks.text: Keep clear of the relief discharge. A drip needs inspection. The cause is unconfirmed. Keep people away and leave the outlet unobstructed. Call a licensed plumber or water heater professional now. Do not lift the lever, cap the pipe, or drain the heater while it is discharging.

chunks.title: Report the unusual noise
chunks.text: Report the unusual noise. Popping or rumbling in a tank is often sediment. It’s common and not an emergency on its own. Not normal if you also see water at the base or a relief pipe that’s running. Stop this check and call a licensed water heater professional if water is also present. For a bang with smoke, gas, or fumes, leave and call from outside. Don’t open the drain valve or try to drain or flush the tank yourself. Do not drain, flush, or reset the heater to investigate.

chunks.title: Care for the burned person first
chunks.text: Care for the burned person first. For a serious burn, call 911. Do not keep testing the hot water. Move away from the hot water. For a serious burn, call 911. Arrange professional inspection before using unusually hot water again. Do not change a gas valve, mixing valve, or hidden thermostat.

chunks.title: Call a plumber about the leak
chunks.text: Call a plumber about the leak. A.O. Smith says condensation on a gas tank usually clears in 1–2 hours (Use and Care 100277666, p. 23). A tank that leaks from its body can’t be patched; the tank has to be replaced. Stay away from water and electrical equipment. Call a licensed plumber or water heater professional promptly. Tell them whether water is spreading. Do not open covers, use the drain valve, or operate the heater’s water valves.

chunks.title: One reset sent
chunks.text: One reset sent. Reset once, only once. If it stops or shows the same code again, don’t reset it again. Repeated shutdowns mean a safety device is doing its job. Call a licensed plumber or water heater professional and tell them the code and what you saw. If the same code comes back, don’t reset it again. Call a licensed plumber or water heater professional and tell them the code and what you saw. Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, drain or fl…

chunks.title: Stop using unexpectedly hot water
chunks.text: Stop using unexpectedly hot water. There is a scalding risk. A displayed setting does not prove the temperature at the tap. Rheem’s chart shows about 30 seconds at 130 °F and less than 5 seconds at 140 °F (p. 18). Keep people away from the hot water and call a licensed plumber or water heater professional. If anyone is burned, care for them first. For a serious burn, call 911. Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, drain or flush, or reset a brea…

chunks.title: The valve opened and closed
chunks.text: The valve opened and closed. The valve opened and closed. Your manual lists how often to repeat this. If the pipe starts dripping later, call a licensed plumber or water heater professional. Leave the lever snapped back. If the pipe starts dripping later, call a licensed plumber or water heater professional. Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, drain or flush, or reset a breaker or safety control.

chunks.title: Vent cleared
chunks.text: Vent cleared. Vent cleared. If hot water hasn’t come back within an hour, call a licensed plumber or water heater professional. If the vent is clear and the code or outage stays, the blockage or fault is inside the vent or the heater. Opening either risks exhaust (carbon monoxide) in the house. If hot water hasn’t come back within an hour, call a licensed plumber or water heater professional. Do not open covers, work on gas or wiring, adjust appliance valves, drain or flush,…

chunks.title: Stop using hot water and get help
chunks.text: Stop using hot water and get help. Soot, exhaust fumes, scorching, or a damaged vent can indicate combustion or venting problems. If there are fumes, a CO alarm, gas smell, smoke, or illness, get everyone out and call 911 from outside. Keep away from the appliance and call a licensed water heater professional for urgent guidance. Do not touch vents, open covers, relight a pilot, or operate gas controls.

chunks.title: Stay away from water and electrical equipment
chunks.text: Stay away from water and electrical equipment. Water near electrical parts or previously flooded equipment must not be used. Stay out of the water and away from the appliance. For sparks, rising water, or immediate danger, leave and call 911 from outside. Call a licensed water heater professional before any use resumes. Do not touch switches, cords, breakers, or the wet equipment.

chunks.title: This sounds like a water odor from the hot water.
chunks.text: This sounds like a water odor from the hot water.. A rotten-egg smell that comes only from the hot water usually comes from the water itself. Sulfate in the water can react with the water heater’s anode rod (a metal rod that protects the tank), and bacteria can make it worse. A water softener can make the anode wear faster. Makers say a different type of anode rod can reduce or end the smell. Ask a licensed plumber or water heater professional to choose and fit the anode you…

chunks.title: If the cold water smells too, the smell is likely in your water supply.
chunks.text: If the cold water smells too, the smell is likely in your water supply.. When both hot and cold water smell, the cause is usually the water coming into the house, not the water heater. If you have a well, have the water tested. If you get city water, call your water utility. If the smell is in the air too, or you’re unsure, treat it as gas: leave the house and call the gas utility or 911 from outside. chunks.title: Parts and electrical repairs are not offered for water-source heat pumps.
chunks.text: Parts and electrical repairs are not offered for water-source heat pumps.. Capacitor, contactor, pump, wiring, and refrigerant work need a trained technician. Leave covers on. Call a pro who works on geothermal or water-source heat pumps. Do not start a parts, electrical, or refrigerant repair from this check.

chunks.title: A breaker that keeps tripping is a stop sign.
chunks.text: A breaker that keeps tripping is a stop sign.. A breaker that will not stay on is protecting the wiring. The cause is in the electrical system, the pump, or the unit. That is not a homeowner repair. Leave the breaker off. Do not reset it again. Set the thermostat to Off. Never heat with an oven, stove, grill, or generator indoors (carbon monoxide). If you use an electric space heater, plug it straight into a wall outlet, follow its maker’s instructions, and keep it clear of…

chunks.title: Get the person warm first.
chunks.text: Get the person warm first.. Someone at risk from cold matters more than the equipment. If anyone is confused, very drowsy, or hard to wake, call 911 now. If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first. Add blankets and dry layers while getting help. Do not open equipment, reset a breaker, change water valves, or work on the well.

chunks.title: The home needs heat. Call for service today.
chunks.text: The home needs heat. Call for service today.. A cold or falling indoor temperature, uncertainty about its trend, or possible freezing pipes needs prompt attention. If the house is getting cold, call a licensed HVAC professional. If it’s dangerously cold and anyone is at risk, get them somewhere warm first. If the house is still getting some heat, leave the thermostat on Heat. If your thermostat has an Emergency Heat setting, switch to it to keep heat on with backup heat whil…

chunks.text: Furnaces, air handlers, and boilers have their own questions.. For gas, oil, electric, or hydronic air heat, use Furnace or air handler on the system-type screen. For a boiler, choose Boiler & hydronic heat. If you smell gas or a carbon monoxide alarm is sounding, leave the building now and call 911 or your gas company from outside. For gas, oil, electric, or hydronic air heat, start again and choose Furnace or air handler. For a boiler, start again and choose Boiler & hydro…

chunks.title: A ductless mini-split has its own check.
chunks.text: A ductless mini-split has its own check.. This check is for water-source and geothermal heat pumps. Mini-split heating and cooling concerns, on one indoor unit or several rooms, start from the home screen. Go back home, press Start, and choose “Ductless mini-split”. If anything is unsafe, use Stop / get help. Do not use these water-source steps on a mini-split.

chunks.title: Visible drain cleared. Watch for water.
chunks.text: Visible drain cleared. Watch for water.. A clog you could already see was cleared. The cause has not been confirmed. Keep water away from wiring. If water reaches electrical parts, use Get help now. If water keeps collecting, call a pro who works on geothermal or water-source heat pumps. Don’t pour chemicals in the drain, and don’t open the unit. Do not open equipment, reset a breaker or disconnect, change water valves, or work on the well.

Give the system about 15 minutes. If airflow or comfort stays poor, call a pro who works on geothermal or water-source heat pumps. Don’t open any other panel, and don’t reset a breaker or disconnect. Do not open equipment, reset a breaker or disconnect, change water valves, or work on the well.

If the house is still getting some heat, leave the thermostat on Heat. If your thermostat has an Emergency Heat setting, switch to it to keep heat on with back…

Gas, a CO alarm, a refrigerant leak alarm, smoke, sparks, a burning smell, flooding, water at electrical equipment, or a breaker that will not stay on is not a do-it-yourself path. If you smell gas or a carbon monoxide alarm is sounding, leave the building and call for help from outside. Do not use switches inside. If there is smoke, fire, or sparks, get everyone out and call 911 from outside. If a refrigerant leak alarm is going off, move peop…

chunks.text: One thermostat reset is done.. The thermostat was turned Off and back On one time. Don’t do that again. Leave the thermostat as it is. Don’t reset it again. If the lockout returns, or there is no warm air, call a pro who works on geothermal or water-source heat pumps. Don’t reset a breaker or disconnect. Do not open equipment, reset a breaker or disconnect, change water valves, or work on the well.

Do not open equipment, reset a breaker or disconnect, change water valves, or work on the well.

chunks.text: Do not walk into water near this equipment.. This system has water pipes, a pump, and 240-volt power in the same space. Standing or spraying water near them can cause a shock. Stay out of the water and keep others away. Turn off the power only if you already know which breaker or disconnect switch feeds this equipment, and you can reach it without touching water or standing in it, opening any panel or box cover (opening the breaker panel’s door is fine), or going near the wa…

chunks.text: Filter and drain looks only. Water care is a pro job.. Open-loop water care stays with a pro. The only homeowner looks are an air filter you can already reach and a condensate drain you can already see. Use only a filter door you already open for a filter change. Don’t open the unit. Look at a drain you can already see. Don’t pour anything into it. Don’t work on the well, the pump, or the pressure tank. Call a pro who services open-loop geothermal systems. Do not open equipm…

Checking and cleaning it takes special equipment and chemicals. This is a reason to call, not a confirmed diagnosis. Leave covers on. Leave water valves, the well, the well pump, and the pressure tank alone. If the house is still getting some heat, leave the thermostat on Heat. Call a technician who works on water-source or geothermal systems of this type. In a business or apartment building, contact the building manager first. If anything becomes unsafe, use Stop / get help. Do n…

chunks.title: We need to know what system you have.
chunks.text: We need to know what system you have.. Guessing the system type could send you to the wrong steps. Do not open covers to find out. Check paperwork, the owner’s manual, or a label you can already see without opening anything. Ask the company that installed or services it. Start again when you know. If you cannot find out, call your HVAC company instead of guessing. Do not remove panels, go into a well pit or crawlspace, or climb to read a model number.

chunks.text: Thermostat setting updated.. You changed a mode or setpoint you could already see. Operation has not been confirmed. Leave the thermostat on the setting you just chose. Give it about 15 minutes. If the home still has the same problem, call a pro who works on geothermal or water-source heat pumps. Don’t open the unit, and don’t reset a breaker or disconnect. chunks.text: Keep the heat pump from running without its water supply.. You reported an open-loop system and weak or missing house well water. Neither the well condition nor water flow through the unit has been confirmed. If the house well water is also out, tell the pro. Until the well works again, set the thermostat to Emergency Heat (it may say Em Heat), not normal Heat. If it has no Emergency Heat setting, set it to Off. In normal Heat the heat pump may still try to run without well…

chunks.title: Breaker rule
chunks.text: You may switch a breaker off. One reset of a tripped outdoor air-conditioner breaker exists only inside the guided check, with the panel cover left on, and only once. If it trips again or will not stay on, leave it off and call a licensed HVAC professional or electrician. Heat pumps, furnaces, boilers, water heaters, and mini-splits do not get a breaker reset here. Never open the breaker panel cover or the disconnect box. Never use a pressure washer on an outdoor unit. It can flatten the fins and damage the coil.

chunks.title: What stays closed
chunks.text: No refrigerant handling, no gas-valve or burner work, no pilot relighting, no opening an electrical panel or disconnect box, no live electrical work, and no bypassing or jumpering a safety control. Covers stay on. Advanced repairs, the equipment catalog, and contractor referrals are off. This is not a review by a licensed HVAC professional or an attorney.

chunks.title: Gas smell and carbon monoxide
chunks.text: If you smell gas or rotten eggs in the air, not just from the hot water, leave the house now and call the gas utility or 911 from outside. Do not touch light switches or phones inside. If a carbon monoxide alarm sounds, or anyone has a headache, dizziness, nausea, or drowsiness, get everyone outside and call 911 from outside. Do not search for the leak. A rotten-egg smell only when the hot water runs is a water problem: /answers/hot-water-rotten-egg-smell/ . Gas, pilot, and flame limits: /answers/gas-smell-pilot-flame/ .

chunks.title: What this guide is
chunks.text: Free informational guidance. Not a licensed HVAC technician, not a diagnosis, and not emergency help. Manufacturer instructions and a professional take priority. Start the guided check at /#/ . Answer pages are at /answers/ .

chunks.title: Smoke, fire, and sparking
chunks.text: If you can see smoke, a smoke alarm is going off, or there is fire or sparking, get everyone outside and call 911 from outside. Do not stay and troubleshoot. A light dusty smell the first time heat runs this season can fade within about an hour. A plastic, rubber, or electrical smell, or a smell that lasts, means turn the heat Off at the thermostat and call a licensed HVAC professional. See /answers/furnace-burning-smell/ .
